definitions.explanation: A suffix attached to numbers to indicate the ordinal period or class session in a school day. For example, 1時間目 means 'first period.'

examples.japanese: {一|いち}{時間目|じかんめ}は{数学|すうがく}だ。
{三|さん}{時間目|じかんめ}の{授業|じゅぎょう}に{遅|おく}れた。
examples.english: I was late for the third-period class.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{六|ろく}{時間目|じかんめ}まであるから、{帰|かえ}りが{遅|おそ}くなる。
examples.english: Today there are classes up to sixth period, so I'll be home late.

notes:
A suffix attached to numbers to indicate ordinal class periods in a school day. Japanese schools typically have 5-6 periods ({時限|じげん}) per day.

COUNTING:
- {一|いち}{時間目|じかんめ}: first period
- {二|に}{時間目|じかんめ}: second period
- {三|さん}{時間目|じかんめ}: third period
- {何|なん}{時間目|じかんめ}: which period?

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {一|いち}{時間目|じかんめ}は{国語|こくご}だ: first period is Japanese language
- {六|ろく}{時間目|じかんめ}まである: there are classes up to sixth period

CONTRAST:
- {時間目|じかんめ}: used in elementary through high school for class periods
- {時限|じげん}: also means "period" (more formal; used in university timetables)
- {限目|げんめ}: abbreviated form of {時限目|じげんめ}, e.g., {一|いち}{限目|げんめ} (first period, college usage)
